newsitem.title: UK: Britain suspects IRA of bomb attack - Mayhew.
newsitem.headline: Britain suspects IRA of bomb attack - Mayhew.

text.p: Britain's Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Patrick Mayhew said on Tuesday the IRA was the prime suspect for the bombing of British army headquarters in the province.

Mayhew told a news conference the attack on the base at Lisburn near Belfast, which injured 20 soldiers and 11 civilians, was "consistent with a terrorist organisation which declared a ceasefire in August 1994".
It was the most explicit condmenation by a British government minister of the Irish Republican Army, which has fought British rule of Northern Ireland for 27 years.
The IRA declared a ceasefire in August 1994 to get its Sinn Fein political wing invited to peace talks but went back to war in February this year.
The IRA has struck at targets on the British mainland and a British army base in Germany since February but has avoided targeting the province itself to date.
No group has yet claimed responsibility for the Lisburn bombing.
Mayhew was speaking after talks with securty chiefs in Belfast on return from a conference in Pittsburgh which is discussing investment in Northern Ireland to consolidate peace.
The Irish Times newspaper quoted security sources as saying only the IRA would have the expertise to carry out the attack.

The guerrillas have over the years fired mortar bombs at the 10 Downing Street London residence of British Prime Minister John Major and launched similar devices at Heathrow airport, the world's busiest.
